relations.subject: tool:cbexport
relations.evidence: This tool supports authenticating against a Couchbase Cluster by using certificate based authentication (mTLS authentication).

relations.subject: tool:cbexport
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate ('the subject offers a closed choice between the named alternative configurations'), applied here to the --format flag's two values
relations.evidence: The lines format specifies a file that contains one JSON document on every line in the file. This format is specified by setting the --format option to "lines".

relations.subject: tool:cbexport
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted, sibling of the lines relation above
relations.evidence: The list format specifies a file which contains a JSON list where each element in the list is a JSON document. The file may only contain a single list, but the list may be specified over multiple lines.

notable_absence.finding: The `_system` scope exclusion is stated as a plain default ('Note that the `_system` scope is not exported by default. To do this use the `--include-data` flag') with no reference to any privilege or role gating why - contrast with the rest of the corpus's system-keyspace pages, which usually pair a `_system`/system-scope restriction with a named privilege (e.g. query_system_catalog). No relation minted since the page states only the default behavior, not a reason.

cross_component_finding: The CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION (MTLS AUTHENTICATION) and HOST FORMATS sections on this page are verbatim-identical to cbdatarecovery.md (earlier in this batch) and cbimport-csv.md/cbimport-json.md (later in this batch) - reused auth-mechanism:x509-certificate consistently across all four rather than minting a per-tool mTLS concept each time. HOST FORMATS itself (connection-string syntax, SRV records, CAO/K8s alternate addressing) is pure CLI flag-syntax documentation with no semantic content beyond string-format rules and was left unextracted here, consistent with prior rounds never having extracted it either (no existing record in the corpus captures 'HOST FORMATS' text at all, checked via grep before deciding not to force a concept for it).
cross_product_finding: Capella's cli-import-export.md and export.md both name cbexport/cbexport json explicitly as the CLI export path (as against the UI/REST Data Tools path), but neither states the lines/list format distinction this page defines - dataset-format:lines and dataset-format:list are first attested here, not on any Capella page.
